```{r phase7_e5}
    # than leaving it to be caught in the standing notes at the end.
    cat(sprintf("%s word list: proportionality present in %.1f%% of non-blank responses%s\n",
                it, 100 * mean(dd$dict_proportionality > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
                ifelse(mean(dd$dict_proportionality > 0, na.rm = TRUE) < .10,
                       "  <- below 10%: read a null here as null-BY-ABSENCE", "")))
  }
}

# H6 itself, from the closed-ended items, as the last row. This is the same
# correlation the main analysis document tests confirmatorily; it appears here so
# the text and survey answers to one question can be read on one line. The
# comparison is qualitative -- do both come out weak? -- not a formal test of
# equality between the two coefficients.
e5_rows[[length(e5_rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(
  stream = "survey (H6 itself)", item = "r(deserved, proportionality_jd)",
  r = bench_h6$r, lo = bench_h6$lo, hi = bench_h6$hi, p = bench_h6$p,
  n = bench_h6$n, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

e5_results <- do.call(rbind, e5_rows)
print(knitr::kable(e5_results, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "E5: do desert and proportionality hold together, in text and in the survey?"))
readr::write_csv(e5_results, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "e5_desert_proportionality.csv"))
```

# PHASE 8: E6 — BACKWARD VERSUS FORWARD WITHIN PERSON

**E6 (exploratory).** Backward-looking explanations (*why this sentence*, Q1) are more
retributive, and forward-looking explanations (*what the sentence should accomplish*, Q2)
more consequentialist. The **within-person** difference
`delta = facet(backward) - facet(forward)` indexes a retributive versus consequentialist
motive.

The pairing is strictly within person: only participants who wrote a non-blank answer to
**both** Q1 and Q2 contribute. Because the two items differ in typical length, the word
count of each response enters as a covariate — the delta is tested both raw (paired *t*)
and adjusted (regression of the delta on the word-count delta).

```{r phase8_e6}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 8: E6 -- BACKWARD MINUS FORWARD, WITHIN PERSON
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: defines run_e6(), which pairs each participant's Q1 and
# Q2 responses, computes the per-facet within-person difference, and tests it
# both raw (paired t) and adjusted for the difference in response length. Runs it
# on the ensemble (the test) and on the word list (corroboration).
# PREREG: 2.4 (E6), 6.7 ("For E6 we compare each person's facets in the
#         backward-looking item with the forward-looking item"), 5.15 (the
#         backward/forward distinction the study is built to keep).
# WRITES: e6_results, e6_dict, e6_all; output/tables/e6_backward_minus_forward.csv;
#         one FAMILY row per facet (ensemble only).
#
# WHY WITHIN PERSON. Comparing the two items BETWEEN people would confound the
# item difference with everything that differs between the people who answered
# each. Every participant supplies both responses, so each acts as their own
# control and stable individual differences in verbosity, vocabulary and
# punitiveness cancel out of the difference. Only participants who wrote a
# non-blank answer to BOTH items contribute.
#
# THE PREDICTION IS SIGNED AND FACET-SPECIFIC: positive deltas for the retributive
# facets (they belong to explaining WHY), negative for the consequentialist ones
# (they belong to explaining WHAT FOR). The `family` column in the output exists
# so the sign can be checked against the prediction facet by facet, and a uniform
# positive delta across all nine would indicate something wrong with the pairing
# rather than support for E6.
#
# GUARD: E_READY for the ensemble arm; DICT_READY for the word-list arm.
# =========================================================================

e6_results <- NULL

#' Run E6 over one facet stream.
#' @param prefix  column prefix identifying the stream: "ens_" or "dict_"
#' @param label   the stream name to print in the `stream` column
#' @return  one row per facet (stream, facet, family, means, delta, t, p, dz,
#'          p_wordadj, n), or NULL if the stream has no facet columns
#'
#' Written as a function because it is run twice on the same logic, once per
#' stream. Only the ensemble run is registered in the FDR family; the word-list
#' run is corroboration, as everywhere else.
run_e6 <- function(prefix, label) {
  cols <- paste0(prefix, FACETS_ALL)
  cols <- intersect(cols, names(facets_joined))
  # No columns for this stream means it has not arrived; the caller handles NULL.
  if (!length(cols)) return(NULL)

  wide <- facets_joined %>%
    # ONLY backward and forward here -- the ranking item is excluded. E6 is
    # specifically the Q1-versus-Q2 contrast: both are about the same sentence
    # this participant just imposed, which is what makes the pair comparable.
    # Q333 is about the goal ranking and belongs to E3, not here.
    dplyr::filter(item_type %in% c("backward", "forward"), nonblank) %>%
    dplyr::select(response_id, item_type, n_words, dplyr::all_of(cols)) %>%
    # Pivot to one row per participant with _backward and _forward variants of
    # every facet AND of n_words. Pivoting n_words alongside the facets is what
    # makes the length-difference covariate available below.
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = item_type,
                       values_from = c(dplyr::all_of(cols), n_words))

  rows <- lapply(cols, function(cc) {
    b <- wide[[paste0(cc, "_backward")]]; f <- wide[[paste0(cc, "_forward")]]
    if (is.null(b) || is.null(f)) return(NULL)
    # complete.cases on the PAIR is the within-person requirement: a participant
    # who answered only one of the two items contributes to neither side.
    ok <- stats::complete.cases(b, f)
    if (sum(ok) < 6) return(NULL)
    delta <- b[ok] - f[ok]
    # A constant difference (usually every delta exactly 0, from a facet neither
    # item ever triggers) has no variance for a paired t to work with.
    if (stats::sd(delta) == 0) return(NULL)
    # A one-sample t on the differences IS the paired t-test, and writing it this
    # way keeps the delta available for the covariate-adjusted model below.
    # Two-sided: the direction of the prediction differs by facet family, so a
    # single one-sided alternative would be wrong for half the rows.
    tt <- stats::t.test(delta)
    # Cohen's dz, the effect size for a within-person design: the mean difference
    # in units of the SD OF THE DIFFERENCES. Not comparable to a between-groups d,
    # because the denominator is a difference SD, which is smaller when the two
    # measures are correlated -- as they are here, both coming from the same
    # person.
    dz <- mean(delta) / stats::sd(delta)

    # Word-count covariate: the delta is re-tested adjusting for how much longer
    # the backward answer was than the forward one. dw is centred so the intercept
    # is the adjusted mean delta at the average length difference.
    # This is prereg 6.7's word-count covariate in its within-person form. People
    # typically write more when justifying a sentence than when saying what it
    # should accomplish, so part of any facet delta could be the length delta
    # rather than a difference in reasoning.
    dw <- wide$n_words_backward[ok] - wide$n_words_forward[ok]
    dw <- dw - mean(dw, na.rm = TRUE)
    m  <- tryCatch(stats::lm(delta ~ dw), error = function(e) NULL)
    # Row 1, column 4 of the coefficient matrix is the p-value for the INTERCEPT,
    # and the intercept is the point of the model: with dw centred, it is the mean
    # delta at the average length difference, so testing it against zero is the
    # length-adjusted version of the paired t. The slope on dw is a nuisance
    # parameter here and is not reported.
    p_adj <- if (!is.null(m)) stats::coef(summary(m))[1, 4] else NA_real_

    # Strip the stream prefix so the `facet` column reads the same for both
    # streams and the two can be stacked and plotted together.
    facet <- sub(paste0("^", prefix), "", cc)
    data.frame(stream = label, facet = facet,
               family = ifelse(facet %in% PRINCIPLED_FACETS, "principled",
                        ifelse(facet %in% VENGEFUL_FACETS, "vengeful", "consequentialist")),
               M_backward = mean(b[ok]), M_forward = mean(f[ok]),
               delta = mean(delta), t = unname(tt$statistic), p = tt$p.value,
               dz = dz, p_wordadj = p_adj, n = sum(ok), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  })
  do.call(rbind, rows)
}

if (E_READY) {
  # The ensemble run is the E6 test, so every facet row is registered.
  e6_results <- run_e6("ens_", "ensemble (LLM)")
  if (!is.null(e6_results)) {
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(e6_results))) {
      # The raw paired-t p is registered rather than p_wordadj: the paired test is
      # the E6 test as prereg 6.7 states it, and the length-adjusted version is
      # reported in the table beside it as a robustness check. Registering both
      # would enter one prediction into the family twice.
      # dz interval uses SE(dz) ~ 1/sqrt(n), the standard large-sample form for a
      # within-person standardized mean difference.
      register_test("E6", sprintf("%s | backward - forward (within person)", e6_results$facet[i]),
                    "dz", e6_results$dz[i],
                    e6_results$dz[i] - 1.96 / sqrt(max(e6_results$n[i], 2)),
                    e6_results$dz[i] + 1.96 / sqrt(max(e6_results$n[i], 2)),
                    e6_results$p[i], e6_results$n[i],
                    claim_eligible = e6_results$facet[i] %in% GATE_PASS)
    }
  }
} else {
  awaiting_colab("E6 (backward vs forward within person, ensemble facets)",
                 c(NLP_FILES[["ensemble"]], NLP_FILES[["agreement"]]))
}

# The word-list run: same function, same logic, different stream. Deliberately
# outside the register_test loop above -- it is corroboration and enters no
# family. bind_rows tolerates either being NULL, so the stacked frame contains
# whichever streams exist and the `stream` column keeps them distinguishable.
e6_dict <- if (DICT_READY) run_e6("dict_", "word list (non-model)") else NULL
e6_all  <- dplyr::bind_rows(e6_results, e6_dict)

if (!is.null(e6_all) && nrow(e6_all)) {
  print(knitr::kable(e6_all, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = "E6: within-person backward minus forward, by facet"))
  readr::write_csv(e6_all, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "e6_backward_minus_forward.csv"))
  cat("\nPrediction: positive deltas for the retributive facets (desert, proportionality,\n")
  cat("censure, moral balance, revenge, suffering) and negative deltas for the\n")
  cat("consequentialist facets (deterrence, incapacitation, rehabilitation).\n")
  if (is.null(e6_results)) {
    cat("Only the non-model word-list stream is present: descriptive, not the E6 test,\n")
    cat("and not registered in the FDR family.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("No E6 stream available yet.\n")
}
```

```{r phase8_e6_figure, fig.height=5}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 8b: FIGURE -- THE E6 DELTAS
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: plots the mean within-person delta per facet, coloured by
# facet family, one panel per stream.
# PREREG: 2.4 (E6). WRITES: output/figures/e6_backward_minus_forward.png
#
# The whole prediction is readable as a shape: principled and vengeful bars above
# the zero line, consequentialist bars below it. Colouring by `family` rather than
# by facet is what makes that pattern visible instead of nine unrelated bars.
# =========================================================================

if (!is.null(e6_all) && nrow(e6_all)) {
  p_e6 <- ggplot2::ggplot(
      # Explicit factor levels keep the facets in scheme order (principled,
      # vengeful, consequentialist) rather than alphabetical, so the predicted
      # sign change falls at one place in the axis.
      e6_all %>% dplyr::mutate(facet = factor(facet, levels = FACETS_ALL)),
      ggplot2::aes(x = facet, y = delta, fill = family)) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = .8), width = .75) +
    # The zero line is the reference the whole prediction is stated against.
    ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
    # One panel per stream with free y scales: ensemble scores and word-list rates
    # per 100 words live on completely different scales, and a shared axis would
    # flatten one of them into a line. What is being compared across panels is the
    # PATTERN of signs, not the magnitudes.
    ggplot2::facet_wrap(~ stream, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    ggplot2::labs(title = "E6: within-person backward minus forward, by facet",
                  subtitle = "Positive = more of this facet when explaining WHY; negative = more when explaining WHAT FOR",
                  x = NULL, y = "mean within-person delta") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
  print(p_e6)
  ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(OUT_FIGURES, "e6_backward_minus_forward.png"),
                  p_e6, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 200)
} else {
  awaiting_colab("The E6 figure", NLP_FILES[["ensemble"]])
}
```

# PHASE 9: E7 — FACETS ADDED TO THE SENTENCE MODEL

**E7 (exploratory).** The language facets add prediction of the within-vignette sentence
**on top of** the survey measures.

> "…we add the facet scores to a model predicting the within-vignette sentence on top of
> the survey measures, using **the eight-item punitiveness scale rather than the full
> index, because the full index already contains the sentence**." — prereg §6.7

The outcome is `Sentence1_z` (standardized within vignette). The baseline predictor is
`punitiveness`, the **eight self-report items**. `punitiveness_full` — which adds
`Sentence1_z` — **must never** appear here, and a hard guard below stops the chunk if it
ever does. Word count is a covariate. Facets are taken from the **backward-looking**
sentence justification (Q1), the response that is actually about this sentence.

```{r phase9_e7_guard}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 9a: THE E7 CIRCULARITY GUARD
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: fixes the E7 baseline predictor set, asserts that nothing
# containing the sentence is in it, and prints both correlations with the outcome
# so the size of the circularity being avoided is on the record.
# PREREG: 6.7 -- "using the eight-item punitiveness scale rather than the full
#         index, because the full index already contains the sentence"; the same
#         principle appears at 5.3 and 5.11 for the sentencing ratio.
# WRITES: E7_BASE_PREDICTORS, FORBIDDEN_IN_E7. Computes no result.
#
# HAZARD, STATED PLAINLY. E7 predicts Sentence1_z. punitiveness_full is the eight
# self-report items PLUS Sentence1_z. Using it as the baseline predictor would put
# the sentence on both sides of the model: the baseline R2 would be inflated by an
# identity rather than by anything anyone measured, and the incremental R2 the
# facets have to beat would be correspondingly meaningless. Use `punitiveness`,
# the eight self-report items, which contains no sentence.
#
# The guard is a stopifnot rather than a comment because a silent version of this
# mistake produces a plausible-looking table. The second stopifnot pair in the
# next chunk re-checks the literal model formulas, so the assertion covers what is
# actually fitted and not merely what was intended.
# =========================================================================

# HARD GUARD: the sentence must not appear on both sides of the model.
E7_BASE_PREDICTORS <- c("sv_punitiveness", "n_words")
# Both the sv_-prefixed and bare names are listed, because the frame carries the
# prefixed form and a hand-edit might reach for the unprefixed one.
FORBIDDEN_IN_E7    <- c("sv_punitiveness_full", "punitiveness_full",
                        "sv_Sentence1", "Sentence1")
stopifnot(!any(FORBIDDEN_IN_E7 %in% E7_BASE_PREDICTORS))
cat("E7 circularity guard: baseline predictors are",
    paste(E7_BASE_PREDICTORS, collapse = " + "), "\n")
cat("  punitiveness (8 self-report items) is used; punitiveness_full is BLOCKED.\n")
# The two correlations are printed side by side as a demonstration. The first is
# a real association between self-reported punitiveness and the sentence someone
# imposed. The second is larger by construction, because Sentence1_z is one of the
# two things averaged into punitiveness_full -- it is partly the sentence
# correlated with itself. Seeing the gap makes the rule self-evidently necessary
# rather than merely asserted.
cat(sprintf("  For reference, r(punitiveness, Sentence1_z) = %.3f and r(punitiveness_full, Sentence1_z) = %.3f\n",
            part_cor(survey$punitiveness, survey$Sentence1_z)$r,
            part_cor(survey$punitiveness_full, survey$Sentence1_z)$r))
cat("  The second number is inflated by construction - that is exactly why it is barred.\n")
```

```{r phase9_e7}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 9b: E7 -- DO THE FACETS ADD TO THE SENTENCE MODEL?
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: fits a survey-only baseline and a survey-plus-facets
# model predicting the within-vignette sentence, and compares them with a nested
# F test. Reports the incremental R2.
# PREREG: 2.4 (E7 -- the facets "add prediction of the sentence beyond the
#         self-report scales"), 6.7 (the eight-item scale, not the full index).
# WRITES: e7_results; output/tables/e7_sentence_model.csv; one FAMILY row.
#
# THE MODELS:
#   baseline  Sentence1_z ~ punitiveness(8 items) + word count
#   full      baseline + the facet scores
# A nested F test is the right comparison because the models are nested by
# construction -- the full model is the baseline plus terms -- so the F is exactly
# a test of whether those added terms explain variance the baseline did not. The
# incremental R2 is the effect size that goes with it.
#
# FACETS COME FROM Q1 ONLY. The sentence justification is the response actually
# about this sentence. Using the ranking explanation would ask whether the way
# someone described their general goals predicts a particular sentence, which is a
# different and weaker question.
#
# GUARD: E_READY -- but note the else branch fits the BASELINE anyway, because it
# uses only survey variables. That is the most useful thing this chunk can do
# before the ensemble arrives: it establishes the R2 the facets will have to
# improve on.
# =========================================================================

e7_results <- NULL

if (E_READY) {

  # Prefer the gate-passing facets: E7 is about whether validated language
  # measures add predictive value, and entering unvalidated facets would let noise
  # inflate R2 through sheer number of predictors.
  e7_facets <- if (length(GATE_PASS)) GATE_PASS else character(0)
  if (!length(e7_facets)) {
    # If nothing passed, the model is still fitted -- but on a fixed, small,
    # theory-chosen set (desert, revenge, suffering: the three facets with survey
    # anchors that bear most directly on sentencing) rather than on all nine, and
    # it is labelled descriptive. Choosing the subset by theory rather than by
    # which facets performed best is what keeps this from becoming a search.
    cat("No facet cleared the 6.7 gate, so E7 is fitted on a fixed, theory-chosen\n")
    cat("set -- desert, revenge, suffering -- as a descriptive model only; it\n")
    cat("supports no claim.\n")
    e7_facets <- intersect(c("desert", "revenge", "suffering"), FACETS_ALL)
  }
  e7_cols <- intersect(paste0("ens_", e7_facets), names(facets_joined))

  dd <- facets_joined %>%
    # Q1 only, and only people who wrote something.
    dplyr::filter(item_type == "backward", nonblank) %>%
    dplyr::select(response_id, n_words, sv_punitiveness, sv_punitiveness_full,
                  sv_Sentence1_z, dplyr::all_of(e7_cols)) %>%
    # LISTWISE COMPLETE, AND IT MUST BE. The two models have to be fitted on
    # exactly the same rows or the R2 difference is not an increment at all -- it
    # would confound the added predictors with a change of sample. Filtering once,
    # up front, guarantees it. (sv_punitiveness_full is selected only so it is
    # visible in the frame; it never enters a formula.)
    dplyr::filter(stats::complete.cases(.))

  # Need more rows than parameters plus a margin, or the full model is unstable.
  if (nrow(dd) > (5 + length(e7_cols))) {
    base_fml <- stats::as.formula("sv_Sentence1_z ~ sv_punitiveness + n_words")
    full_fml <- stats::as.formula(paste("sv_Sentence1_z ~ sv_punitiveness + n_words +",
                                        paste(e7_cols, collapse = " + ")))
    # Re-assert the guard on the literal formulas that will be fitted.
    # The Phase 9a assertion checked the intended predictor list; this one checks
    # the strings that actually go to lm(), which is where the circularity would
    # have to show up if it were ever introduced by an edit to the formula rather
    # than to the list.
    stopifnot(!grepl("punitiveness_full", paste(deparse(base_fml), collapse = " ")))
    stopifnot(!grepl("punitiveness_full", paste(deparse(full_fml), collapse = " ")))

    m_base <- stats::lm(base_fml, data = dd)
    m_full <- stats::lm(full_fml, data = dd)
    # anova() on two nested lm objects gives the partial F for the added block.
    cmp <- stats::anova(m_base, m_full)

    # Row 2 of the anova table is the comparison row (row 1 describes the baseline
    # alone). delta_r2 is the plain R2 difference rather than adjusted R2, because
    # the F test already accounts for the number of added parameters and the two
    # would otherwise penalise the same thing twice.
    delta_r2 <- summary(m_full)$r.squared - summary(m_base)$r.squared
    f_stat <- cmp$F[2]; p_val <- cmp$`Pr(>F)`[2]

    cat("\n--- Baseline: survey only (8-item punitiveness + word count) ---\n")
    print(summary(m_base)$coefficients)
    cat(sprintf("R2 = %.4f\n", summary(m_base)$r.squared))
    cat("\n--- Full: survey + language facets ---\n")
    print(summary(m_full)$coefficients)
    cat(sprintf("R2 = %.4f\n", summary(m_full)$r.squared))
    cat(sprintf("\nIncremental R2 from the facets: %.4f, F(%d, %d) = %.3f, p %s\n",
                delta_r2, cmp$Df[2], cmp$Res.Df[2], f_stat, format_p(p_val)))

    e7_results <- data.frame(
      model = c("survey only", "survey + facets"),
      predictors = c(paste(deparse(base_fml), collapse = ""),
                     paste(deparse(full_fml), collapse = "")),
      r2 = c(summary(m_base)$r.squared, summary(m_full)$r.squared),
      delta_r2 = c(NA_real_, delta_r2), F = c(NA_real_, f_stat),
      p = c(NA_real_, p_val), n = nrow(dd), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    print(knitr::kable(e7_results, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
                       caption = "E7: do the facets add to the sentence model beyond the 8-item punitiveness scale?"))
    readr::write_csv(e7_results, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "e7_sentence_model.csv"))

    # CI left NA: an incremental R2 has no simple closed-form interval, and the
    # F test with its exact p is the inference here. The registry allows NA
    # bounds for exactly this case.
    # claim_eligible only if something cleared the gate -- an R2 increment from
    # unvalidated facets shows that the text contains SOMETHING predictive, not
    # that the retributive facets do.
    register_test("E7", "facets added to Sentence1_z ~ punitiveness(8) + word count",
                  "delta R2", delta_r2, NA_real_, NA_real_, p_val, nrow(dd),
                  claim_eligible = length(GATE_PASS) > 0)
  } else {
    cat("Too few complete cases for the E7 model.\n")
  }

} else {
  awaiting_colab("E7 (facets added to the sentence model beyond the 8-item punitiveness scale)",
                 c(NLP_FILES[["ensemble"]], NLP_FILES[["agreement"]]))
  # The baseline is computable now and worth printing: it is the bar the facets
  # will have to clear, and knowing it in advance is the difference between
  # reading a future incremental R2 as impressive or as trivial.
  cat("\nThe baseline half of E7 uses only survey variables and can be shown now:\n")
  dd0 <- facets_joined %>%
    # Same filters as the full analysis (Q1, non-blank, complete cases) so this
    # baseline is directly comparable to the one that will be fitted later, not a
    # different model on a different sample.
    dplyr::filter(item_type == "backward", nonblank) %>%
    dplyr::select(n_words, sv_punitiveness, sv_Sentence1_z) %>%
    dplyr::filter(stats::complete.cases(.))
  # Note the predictor: sv_punitiveness, the eight self-report items. Same rule as
  # the guarded branch -- the full index is barred here too.
  m0 <- stats::lm(sv_Sentence1_z ~ sv_punitiveness + n_words, data = dd0)
  print(summary(m0)$coefficients)
  cat(sprintf("Baseline R2 = %.4f (n = %d). The facets will be added to THIS model.\n",
              summary(m0)$r.squared, nrow(dd0)))
}
```

```{r phase9_e7_secondary}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 9c: THE SECONDARY E7 CHECKS
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: correlates the two vengeful facets with the shark pain
# rating and with the sentence, word count partialled.
# PREREG: 6.7 -- "We also report whether revenge and suffering language predict
#         the shark pain rating and the sentence."
# WRITES: printed table only. Registers NOTHING -- the prereg says "report",
#         which is a descriptive instruction, and E7's registered test is the
#         incremental R2 above.
#
# WHY THE SHARK. Shark_3 asks how painful the animal's death should be
# (prereg 5.10). A shark cannot be deterred, reformed or held responsible, so no
# forward-looking justification and no Kantian desert claim applies to it: wanting
# its death to hurt is close to a pure measure of the appetite for suffering.
# Vengeful LANGUAGE tracking that rating would be striking convergence between two
# very different measurements of the same disposition.
#
# GUARD: E_READY plus the presence of sv_Shark_3, which is optional in the scored
# file (see the any_of() in Phase 3f).
# =========================================================================

# Secondary E7 question from prereg 6.7: "We also report whether revenge and
# suffering language predict the shark pain rating and the sentence."
if (E_READY && "sv_Shark_3" %in% names(facets_joined)) {
  dd <- facets_joined %>% dplyr::filter(item_type == "backward", nonblank)
  sec <- lapply(intersect(paste0("ens_", VENGEFUL_FACETS), names(dd)), function(cc) {
    # `a` is the shark-pain correlation, `b` the sentence correlation. Both are
    # partial on word count, and n is reported separately for each because
    # Shark_3 is only answered by participants who said the shark should be
    # killed, so its n is the smaller of the two.
    a <- part_cor(dd[[cc]], dd$sv_Shark_3, dd$n_words)
    b <- part_cor(dd[[cc]], dd$sv_Sentence1_z, dd$n_words)
    data.frame(facet = sub("^ens_", "", cc),
               r_shark_pain = a$r, p_shark = a$p, n_shark = a$n,
               r_sentence_z = b$r, p_sentence = b$p, n_sentence = b$n)
  })
  if (length(sec)) {
    print(knitr::kable(do.call(rbind, sec), digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
                       caption = "Secondary: does vengeful language predict the shark pain rating and the sentence?"))
  }
} else {
  awaiting_colab("The secondary E7 checks (vengeful language -> shark pain rating, sentence)",
                 NLP_FILES[["ensemble"]])
}
```

# PHASE 10: BENJAMINI–HOCHBERG FDR WITHIN THE E3–E7 FAMILY

> "E3 through E7 form **one exploratory family**; we control the false discovery rate
> within it and report effect sizes and confidence intervals." — prereg §6.7

The correction is applied **within** this family and nowhere else. These are **exploratory**
tests: nothing here is confirmatory, and no result here is combined with the confirmatory
H1–H21 family in the main analysis document. Descriptive results — the word-list previews,
base-rate reports, the holistic "both" rate — are deliberately excluded from the family so
they neither borrow nor lend power.

```{r phase10_fdr}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 10: BENJAMINI-HOCHBERG ACROSS THE E3-E7 FAMILY
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: applies BH-FDR to every p-value in the FAMILY registry,
# sorts by raw p, prints the family, and counts how many survive at q = .05 --
# separating the survivors that are claim-eligible under the 6.7 gate from those
# that are not.
# PREREG: 2.4 and 6.7 -- "E3 through E7 form one exploratory family; we control
#         the false discovery rate within it and report effect sizes and
#         confidence intervals." Threshold alpha = .05 per prereg 6.8.
# WRITES: FAMILY gains p_BH and sig_BH; output/tables/e3_e7_family_fdr.csv.
#
# WHY BH RATHER THAN BONFERRONI. These are exploratory tests whose purpose is to
# identify effects worth pursuing. Controlling the family-wise error rate would
# be the right instrument if a single false positive anywhere invalidated the set;
# controlling the FALSE DISCOVERY RATE -- the expected share of claimed effects
# that are false -- is the right one when the output is a list of candidates. It
# is also far less conservative across a family this size, and BH is what the
# prereg specifies here and at 6.1 for the H1 correlation set.
#
# ACROSS EXACTLY WHICH SET. The registry, and only the registry: the tests of E3,
# E4, E5, E6 and E7, which are ONE family. Not across the descriptive results
# (word-list previews, base rates, co-firing rates, the facet-by-facet E4
# decomposition, the secondary shark checks) -- none of those were registered, and
# adding them would enlarge the denominator with results nobody claims from. And
# not across the confirmatory H1-H21 family in the main analysis document, which
# gets its own corrections over its own sets.
#
# EXPLORATORY THROUGHOUT. A row surviving BH here is an exploratory finding.
# Nothing in this document is confirmatory.
# =========================================================================

if (nrow(FAMILY) > 0) {
  # p.adjust(method = "BH") returns adjusted p-values that may be compared
  # directly against q = .05; no separate step-up bookkeeping is needed. NA
  # p-values (a test that could not be computed) pass through as NA and are
  # excluded from the adjustment, which is correct -- a test that did not run is
  # not a test that failed.
  FAMILY$p_BH <- stats::p.adjust(FAMILY$p, method = "BH")
  # Stars on the ADJUSTED p, not the raw one, so the printed table cannot be
  # skimmed for significance that the correction has already removed.
  FAMILY$sig_BH <- ifelse(is.na(FAMILY$p_BH), "", sig_stars(FAMILY$p_BH))
  # Sorted by raw p, which is the order the BH step-up procedure itself works in,
  # so the table reads in the same sequence the correction applied.
  FAMILY <- FAMILY[order(FAMILY$p), ]

  print(knitr::kable(FAMILY, digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
                     caption = "The E3-E7 exploratory family with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control"))
  readr::write_csv(FAMILY, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "e3_e7_family_fdr.csv"))

  # Family size is printed because BH's severity depends on it: the same raw p
  # survives or does not depending on how many tests it sits among, so the
  # denominator belongs in the output next to the result.
  cat(sprintf("\nFamily size: %d tests across %s.\n", nrow(FAMILY),
              paste(sort(unique(FAMILY$hypothesis)), collapse = ", ")))
  # q = .05 matches the alpha of prereg 6.8; under BH it means that among the
  # tests declared here, about 5% are expected to be false discoveries.
  cat(sprintf("Surviving BH at q = .05: %d\n", sum(FAMILY$p_BH < .05, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("  ... of which claim-eligible under the 6.7 gate: %d\n",
              sum(FAMILY$p_BH < .05 & FAMILY$claim_eligible, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat(sprintf("  ... descriptive only (facet did not clear the gate): %d\n",
              sum(FAMILY$p_BH < .05 & !FAMILY$claim_eligible, na.rm = TRUE)))
  cat("\nBH is applied across the whole E3-E7 family, gate-passing or not: the prereg\n")
  cat("defines the family as E3 through E7, and correcting over the larger set is the\n")
  cat("conservative choice. The gate then decides what a surviving test may be used\n")
  cat("FOR - a survivor on a non-gate-passing facet is reported and supports no claim.\n")
  cat("\nAll of these are EXPLORATORY (prereg 2.4). None is labelled confirmatory.\n")
} else {
  cat("The E3-E7 family registry is empty: no test has been run yet.\n\n")
  awaiting_colab("The BH-FDR correction across the E3-E7 exploratory family",
                 c(NLP_FILES[["ensemble"]], NLP_FILES[["agreement"]]))
  cat("\nWhen the ensemble arrives, the family will contain, per gate-passing facet:\n")
  cat("  E3  2 backward items x facets x {group contrast, continuous regression}\n")
  cat("  E4  the principled x vengeful partial correlation, per backward item\n")
  cat("  E5  the desert x proportionality partial correlation, per backward item\n")
  cat("  E6  the within-person backward-minus-forward test, per facet\n")
  cat("  E7  the incremental R2 of the facets over the 8-item punitiveness scale\n")
  cat("and Benjamini-Hochberg is applied across that set and only that set.\n")
  # Write an empty, correctly-shaped family table so downstream tooling has a target.
  # Zero rows but the full column schema, matching the populated version exactly,
  # so a script that reads this CSV works in both states.
  readr::write_csv(FAMILY, file.path(OUT_TABLES, "e3_e7_family_fdr.csv"))
}
```

# PHASE 11: EXPORT, PLACEHOLDERS, SESSION INFO

```{r phase11_export}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 11a: EXPORT INVENTORY AND THE PARTICIPANT-LEVEL FEATURE FILE
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: lists everything the knit wrote, and exports the joined
# facet features for downstream use.
# PREREG: 6.7 -- "The model set and versions, the scoring prompts, the word lists,
#         the raw model output, and the analysis code go on the project's OSF
#         page."
# WRITES: data/cleaned/retribution_nlp_features.csv (only if a facet stream
#         exists).
# =========================================================================

# Listed by scanning the directories rather than from a hard-coded manifest, so
# the inventory reflects what was actually written on this run -- including
# nothing at all, when the whole language side is awaiting Colab.
written <- list.files(OUT_TABLES, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE)
figs    <- list.files(OUT_FIGURES, pattern = "\\.png$", full.names = TRUE)

cat("Tables written to output/tables/:\n")
if (length(written)) for (f in written) cat(sprintf("  %s\n", basename(f))) else cat("  (none)\n")
cat("\nFigures written to output/figures/:\n")
if (length(figs)) for (f in figs) cat(sprintf("  %s\n", basename(f))) else cat("  (none)\n")

# Participant-level facet features for downstream use, whenever any stream exists.
# The prefix pattern is what makes this generic: whichever of the three streams
# arrived contributes its columns, and the export shape follows the inputs.
feature_cols <- grep("^(ens_|dict_|emb_)", names(facets_joined), value = TRUE)
if (length(feature_cols)) {
  nlp_features <- facets_joined %>%
    # Non-blank rows only, and NO sv_* columns: this file carries scored text
    # plus its keys and its word count, nothing from the survey. The survey side
    # already has its own file, and keeping the two separate means neither can be
    # mistaken for the other or joined to itself.
    dplyr::filter(nonblank) %>%
    dplyr::select(response_id, item_type, n_words, dplyr::all_of(feature_cols))
  readr::write_csv(nlp_features, file.path(OUT_DATA, "retribution_nlp_features.csv"))
  cat(sprintf("\nWrote %s (%d rows x %d cols)\n",
              file.path(OUT_DATA, "retribution_nlp_features.csv"),
              nrow(nlp_features), ncol(nlp_features)))
} else {
  cat("\nNo facet features to export yet.\n")
}
```

```{r phase11_placeholders}
# =========================================================================
# PHASE 11b: OUTSTANDING INPUTS AND THE STANDING INTERPRETIVE NOTES
# -------------------------------------------------------------------------
# WHAT THIS CHUNK DOES: restates which of the six Colab inputs are present and
# what each one blocks, then records the interpretive commitments that hold
# whatever the data turn out to say.
# PREREG: 6.7 throughout; 4.4 (the stopping rule).
# WRITES: printed table and notes only.
#
# The notes below are decided in advance on purpose. Two of them -- that censure
# and moral balance stay descriptive, and that a proportionality rate under 10%
# makes E5 a null-by-absence -- are rules about how a result WILL be read, and a
# rule of that kind is only worth anything if it is fixed before the number is
# known.
# =========================================================================

cat("=== WHAT IS STILL A PLACEHOLDER ===\n\n")
# Each row pairs a file with what it blocks, so the table reads as a dependency
# list rather than an inventory: the cost of each missing input is stated in terms
# of the analysis it prevents.
placeholders <- data.frame(
  item = c("ensemble_facet_scores.csv", "ensemble_agreement.csv",
           "embedding_facet_similarity.csv", "facet_dictionary_scores.csv",
           "gold_codes.csv", "gold_split_assignment.csv"),
  needed_for = c("E3, E4, E5, E6, E7 (all primary facet tests)",
                 "gate clause A (inter-model ICC >= .60)",
                 "convergence reporting only (never a gate)",
                 "the non-model corroboration E4 requires",
                 "human-anchored validation of the ensemble",
                 "the frozen SEED/TEST split behind every validation number"),
  status = c(ifelse(ENS_READY, "present", "AWAITING"),
             ifelse(AGREE_READY, "present", "AWAITING"),
             ifelse(EMB_READY, "present", "AWAITING"),
             ifelse(DICT_READY, "present", "AWAITING"),
             ifelse(GOLD_READY, "present", "AWAITING"),
             ifelse(SPLIT_READY, "present", "AWAITING")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
print(knitr::kable(placeholders, row.names = FALSE))

cat("\nOther standing notes:\n")
cat("  - Censure and moral balance have no admissible survey anchor, so they can never\n")
cat("    clear gate clause B. They stay exploratory descriptives by design, not by\n")
cat("    accident, and are reported as such however the data come out.\n")
cat("  - Proportionality language is rare. If its realized non-zero rate in the\n")
cat("    backward-looking items stays below 10%, E5 is reported as a descriptive\n")
cat("    null-by-absence rather than as an orthogonality result.\n")
cat("  - The human gold codes are the strongest non-model anchor for E4; until they\n")
cat("    arrive, the word list is the only non-model stream available.\n")
cat("  - Full dataset (N = 948 after exclusions). Collection is complete, so the\n")
cat("    preregistered tests are the single run the stopping rule in prereg 4.4\n")
cat("    provides for.\n")
```
